governanceNotes: D1 batch 47 (2026-09-24): deferred. Manifestation-identity screen recorded 2026-09-24: (i) the catalog identity is a generic dermatologic sign rather than a specific disease, and the located literature concerns defined pigmentary diseases and exposures - vitiligo reviews and pathogenesis papers, post-inflammatory hypopigmentation in defined dermatoses, and drug-induced or disease-site pigment loss - so applying those results to the generic identity would be an entity mismatch and would also duplicate the catalog's dedicated vitiligo identity, which already authors its own depressive-disorder window (entity-mismatch, synonym-identity, and parallel-pathway guards); (ii) the nearest catalog-fit targets for a pigmentary-disorder psychosocial window are depressive-disorder and anxiety-disorder, whose incoming windows are owned by defined primary dermatoses (vitiligo, alopecia-areata, acne-scarring, hidradenitis-suppurativa, dermatitis), not by a generic sign, and no condition-specific hypopigmentation-primary psychosocial quantification was located (zero-record and duplicate-scope guards); (iii) no secondary-skin-infection, endocrine, nutritional, or malignancy edge was authored - hypopigmentation is a downstream manifestation of those primaries (hypopituitarism, hypothyroidism, nutritional deficiency, mycosis fungoides, therapy-related) rather than their cause, so the direction would be inverted (direction-inversion guard); (iv) this disposition mirrors the batch-46 hyperpigmentation deferral so that the two generic pigmentary-sign identities are treated consistently pending a governance decision. Reopening condition: a generic-hypopigmentation-primary evidence base with a catalog-fit outcome, or a governance decision that narrows this identity to a specific pigmentary disorder.
